Peugeot Expands 208 and 2008 Lineups With New Envy Trim Level
7 photos
Photo: Peugeot
Peugeot has decided to make its aging 208 and 2008 lineups a bit more exciting with the introduction of a new trim level called Envy.
Announced by the company’s UK branch, the grade is based on the Allure specification, and as you can assume, it brings a few upgrades both inside and out.
For instance, aluminum door sills that feature the company’s lettering, and glossy black daytime running light surrounds are some of the novelties. On top of these, the 208 hatchback now comes with 16-inch diamond-cut wheels with a Black Mist Varnish. The Noma alloys are joined by glossy black highlights on the front and rear bumpers, and a Black Diamond roof said to be unique to this model.
As for the Peugeot 2008 crossover, it now comes with a set of 17-inch diamond-cut wheels with a Black Mist varnish. The alloys are called Karakoy, the press release reveals. Both models are also available in new exterior colors that are offered as standard. These include the Alvao Green on the supermini and the Nazaro Blue on the subcompact crossover, with the Lion brand stating that other paint finishes are also available for the two.
Usually found from the GT grade upward, the Dynamic front seats can be seen on the inside, wrapped in Tremezzo embossed fabric, which is said to be new. The Opalite stitching is also on deck, and the Peugeot shield is printed on the headrests at the front. The Opalite decorative stitching and co-ordinated inserts can be found on the enhanced door cards, and the Mistral Black roof lining is also a thing on the new Envy trim level.
Photo: Peugeot The equipment list has also been boosted, with the Envy versions of the Peugeot 208 and 2008 being offered with a 180-degree color reversing camera, and keyless entry and go. Moreover, the crossover is also offered with a two-position trunk floor. These add up to the gear found on the Allure grade, which includes stuff such as the head-up digital gauge cluster, and the Peugeot i-Cockpit, as well as the tinted rear windows, and parking sensors at both ends.
Pricing for the 2026 Peugeot 208 Envy starts at 23,115 pounds (equal to $30,760) on-the-road for the Turbo 100 six-speed manual powertrain. The trim level is also available with the Hybrid 110 e-DSC6 assembly, priced from 24,915 ($33,155), as well as the Electric 50 kWh 136 zero-emission powertrain, with pricing starting at 25,565 pounds ($34,020), or 24,065 pounds ($32,025) after the ECG (Electric Car Grant).
As for the 2026 Peugeot 2008 Envy, it can be ordered from 26,165 pounds ($34,820) for the Turbo 100 six-speed manual, and 29,215 pounds ($38,880) for the Hybrid 145 e-DSC6. Moreover, it is also available with the 1.2-liter PureTech 136 eight-speed automatic assembly, with an on-the-road starting price of 28,465 pounds ($37,880), and in the Electric 54 kWh 156 configuration, priced from 29,965 pounds ($39,880), or 28,465 pounds ($37,880) after the ECG.
It is worth noting that since the new Envy grade version of the Peugeot 208 builds on the Allure, it obvious slots between this variant and the superior GT, whereas the Style is found at the bottom end of the lineup, and the GT Premium tops the family. The Peugeot 2008 lineup includes the Allure, Envy, GT, and GT Premium in the United Kingdom, the company’s official local website reveals.
Photo: Peugeot
The E-208, aka the electric version of the supermini, is available in the Allure, Envy, GT, and GT Premium configurations, as well as the new E-208 GTi , with its 277 hp (281 ps/207 kW) and 254 lb-ft (345 Nm) of torque available on tap, which enables 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) in 5.5 seconds. This model has a WLTP range of 233 miles (375 km) with the battery fully charged. As for the E-2008, it is available in the Allure, Envy, GT, and GT Premium trim levels in the UK.
Peugeot’s portfolio also includes the 308 SW, 3008, 408,, 5008, Rifter, and Traveler in the United Kingdom, and depending on the model, they can be ordered either with gasoline, hybrid, of fully electric firepower.
As a reminder, the second-generation Peugeot 208 has been around since 2019, and that is also when its crossover sibling was introduced. Both models are based on the CMP platform, and other vehicles sharing the same underpinnings are the Jeep Avenger, the Opel / Vauxhall Corsa F and Mokka B, the Fiat 600, DS 3 Crossback, Citroen C4 and C4 X, Lancia Ypsilon, and Alfa Romeo Junior, among others. The Dongfeng Aeolus Yixuan and Yixuan GS are also based on this construction.
The Peugeot 2008 was facelifted in May 2023, and its hatchback sibling followed in its footsteps two months later, in July. The updates include the usual revisions on the outside, some tweaks in the cabin, and a few other novelties meant to keep the two models on the appealing side of their classes for a few more years.
